item.title: Solved: How to Parse Configuration Files, Environment, and Command-Line Arguments in Python
item.description:
Question:

How can one effectively parse configuration files, environment variables, and command-line arguments in Python to achieve a cascading collection of options? The core requirements for this solution include:

  • A structured cascade for option values:
    • Start with default option values, then allow for:
      • Config file options,
      • Environment variables, and finally,
      • Command-line options to override the previous options.
  • The ability to specify multiple configuration file locations directly via the command line using an argument like --config-file foo.conf, ensuring these files are read respecting the defined cascade.
  • An imperative to define option behaviors in one consolidated location, allowing clarity in parsing logic for both configuration files and command-line inputs.
  • The necessity to unify parsed options into a single, easily accessible collection of option values for later use throughout the application without needing to trace back their origin.

With these demands in mind, what is the optimal way to leverage Python’s standard library tools for seamless integration?
